issue_context.title: [Compatibility Version] kube version validation should be moved out of component base
issue_context.body:
xref: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/128279/files#r1890633759

> is k8s.io/component-base supposed to be agnostic for in-tree or out-of-tree components? trying to make sure the n-3 / 1.31 floor we set here is enforced for ValidateKubeEffectiveVersion but wouldn't break a different component with a different versioning scheme from using this package

ref: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/128279#discussion_r1890662857

> Can we open an issue to move this logic out of component-base as well? I would expect k8s components (kube-apiserver, ...) to set the limit according to the rules of that component (N-3 for k8s components), but leave it up to 3rd party component owners to decide what the limit should be for their components.

review_comments:
I'm trying to understand the order of operations here, and the interaction between the optional emulation version and feature gates set by the specific test calling StartTestServer

First we grab a copy of the feature gates cloned from the global gate state
```
featureGate := feature.DefaultMutableFeatureGate.DeepCopy()
```

This is *before* being informed by any `--feature-gates=...` or `--emulate-version` options set in `customFlags`, right?

Then below we call `fs.Parse(customFlags)`... is that step the point at which the local `featureGate` / `effectiveVersion` / `componentGlobalsRegistry` variables are informed by by any `--feature-gates=...` or `--emulate-version` options set in `customFlags`?

Then after that point, we check for any changes in `featureGate` and propagate that back into the global feature gate using SetFeatureGateDuringTest?

Yes, your understanding is correct. We are doing this because setting the emulation version flag would change the feature gate, but it would not be unset/undone at the end of test. 
so 
1. `featureGate := feature.DefaultMutableFeatureGate.DeepCopy()` is to copy all the registered feature gates to local `featureGate`
2. `fs.Parse(customFlags)` and `componentGlobalsRegistry.Set()` sets the local feature gate values.
3. the local feature gate values gets copied to the global feature gate
4. at the end of test, the global feature gate gets unset/undone.
note to self/reviewers: This is not needed anymore because we are setting emulation version via flags.
does flag-set emulated-version set up inside StartTestServer get reset / undone at the end of the test?
the feature gates get reset/undone. EffectiveVersion is a local instance, so it does not need to be reset/undone
nit: copyright year should only change if it's a new file, not just moved and edited.

ah, I see. 
Fixed.

I'm not sure if we should be comparing to the global feature gate state, or a copy of `featureGate` prior to parsing custom flags and setting emulation version. I think comparing to global feature gate state might be a subtle race condition if multiple tests are running in parallel.

Same comment applies elsewhere.

I think it is better to use the global feature gate here. 
If using the local feature gate, if the EmulationVersion  of the global feature gate is changed somewhere else, the test would not be able to see that. 
On the other hand, if a diff is found when comparing to the global feature gate, `SetFeatureGateEmulationVersionDuringTest` and `SetFeatureGateDuringTest` will prevent the parallel override

given we still copy the new feature values back to the DefaultFeatureGate because most feature checks still use the DefaultFeatureGate, I'm a little confused about how we don't still have parallel test issues

`SetFeatureGateDuringTest` has a lock. 
As https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/128163 mention, a lock can solve the problem.
where does this validation move to?
`ValidateKubeEffectiveVersion` validates the version range. It is moved to `func (m *effectiveVersion) Validate()` with `emulationVersionFloor`
And that's getting called from `componentGlobalsRegistry#Validate()`?
yes, that's getting called from componentGlobalsRegistry#Validate()
Why remove this? Will we always default to latest binary version?

It is weird to be able to change the binary version in tests, but it was a hack to test the range of emulation version. Now we are not restricting the range of emulation version in integration test, this is not needed anymore.

If we add a new field or CEL function or something, default n-1 compatibility version means I won't be able to set or use it in the first release, right?

How would someone adjust config to allow use of that in tests? artificially push binaryVersion into the future? override default compatibility version to 1.n?

In the next release, we plan to add flag to set `minCompatibility` version, so that it can be set to 1.n. 
Would there be cases where you want to set it beyond 1.n?

> Would there be cases where you want to set it beyond 1.n?

No, if we had the ability to set min compatibility for tests so we can test things added in *this* release, that's sufficient.

> In the next release, we plan to add flag to set `minCompatibility` version, so that it can be set to 1.n.

I can't tell if removing this before adding minCompatibility control makes it impossible to test some things added in the current release (like CEL functions).
I think you are right. We might need to set the BinaryVersion when setting the minCompatibility. Keeping the option now.

I love seeing this get dropped

edit: oh... it just moved to staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/util/compatibility/registry.go 😆
yeah, at least moving it out of component-base is a step forward? 😆

note to self/reviewers: This is a bug discovered in https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/128279#discussion_r1908013803. Emulation version could have been changed by the previous test and must be reset so this needs to run for all tests rather than selectively calling the function.
where does this validation move to?
`ValidateKubeEffectiveVersion` validates the version range. It is moved to `func (m *effectiveVersion) Validate()` with `emulationVersionFloor`
question, is this constant floating (as it will need to be updated later)? or will be 1.31 forever?
it is tied to the Beta stage of `CustomResourceFieldSelectors`. After 3 releases of `CustomResourceFieldSelectors` GA, this test can be removed.
Can be, or _has_ to be? (and will start failing ...)
(Are we expecting this will be updated in the PR that removes the featuregate codepath? IE this is not a "time bomb" even though it has a hardcoded version? -- Just clarifying)
it is Can be. As long as the `CustomResourceFieldSelectors=false` logic is not cleaned up, this test would not fail. If there is code clean up, this test should be cleaned up as well.
Thanks. @aojea IMHO we can resolve this thread?
add a comment explaining the rationale of this , is this n-2  with n being the current version?
Added a comment.
is the reason this is safe to drop because this test isn't setting emulated version or feature gates that differ per test?
still had this question
this is safe to drop because of existing lock in feature gates. There is no more tests changing the feature gates without being guarded by the lock.

I'm trying to understand the registry plumbing this PR does in the server startup... there's still a global, but now there's also an instance variable in ServerRunOptions? I'm a little confused about why we have a global and a plumbed instance var, and when we're supposed to use which

Ideally we do not want to use a global so that we can set the registry independently for tests. In the last 4 commits, I have removed most references to `DefaultComponentGlobalsRegistry` except in cmd options, and cel `DefaultCompatibilityVersion()`. We still need it because it is tricky to pass it into cel right now. We can address it in a followup.
